Sleep: The highest-return item in this workbook
9 hours per night (the original sheet said 'per week' - assuming typo)
22:00 / 07:00, seven days a week including weekends
Consistent wake time. Consistency beats duration if you have to pick one.
Sleep debt blunts training adaptation, appetite regulation, and skin recovery simultaneously - it undercuts every other tab.
Eating: Phase 1: 160 -> 175 lbs. Surplus is the mechanism; consistency is the constraint.
~0.94 g/lb at 160 lbs. No reason to go higher.
Do not cut this to make room for carbs - it is hormone and calorie insurance.
The lever. Add carbs first when the scale stalls.
Floor, not a target. At 4,000 kcal this is easy to miss.
Grams are the inputs (blue-editable); calories and % recalculate.
Let the scale settle, let appetite reset

An hour of goalkeeping every day is roughly 300-500 kcal you were not previously spending. If the scale stops moving for two consecutive Monday weigh-ins, add ~300 kcal (75g carbs) rather than cutting the GK session.
Goalkeeping: 1 hour daily. Warm-up 10 / technical 20 / main 25 / cool-down 5.
Lofted serves to catch at full extension, back-pedal and set, claim through contact. 4 x 8 reps with a full reset between.
Footwork ladder, set position under a moving ball, W-catch repetition, low blocks from the knees. Deliberately unloaded.
Low and mid-height shots from 12-16 yards. Collapse dive mechanics: lead hand first, no rolling onto the shoulder.
Throws (roll, javelin, overarm) to targets at 20/30/40 yards. Goal kicks both feet. Driven ball under a 3-second clock.
Deflected and screened shots, close-range rebound work, double-save sequences. Short reps, long rests.
Near-post and far-post service, punch vs. catch decisions, starting position off the line. Call it every time.
Onrushing attacker from three angles. Spread late, stay big, hands low. Recovery saves after a first touch beats you.
- Never dive cold. The 10-minute warm-up is not optional and it is where most keeper injuries are avoided.
- Sunday is technical only. Seven hard days a week is how you arrive at Phase 2 injured instead of 15 lbs heavier.
- Goalkeeping goes BEFORE the lift, not after. Skill work on fatigued legs teaches bad mechanics.
- If a session has to be cut, cut the main block and keep the technical block. Reps of the fundamentals compound.
- Fingers, wrists and hips get the cool-down. They take the load nobody budgets for.

RIR = reps in reserve. In the original file these were stored as dates - Excel converted '2-3' to 3 Feb 2026 and '1-2' to 2 Jan 2026. Fixed here as text.
+5 lbs upper body, +10 lbs lower body once you hit the top of the rep range at the target RIR. If you miss two sessions in a row on a lift, deload it 10% and build back.
Wednesday and Saturday. 20-25 min, Zone 2, conversational pace. If you cannot talk through it, you are going too hard - this is recovery and aerobic base, not a workout.
Posture: POSTURE
Anchor to a cue, not a clock.
CUE 1 - AMPLITUDE, NOT TEMPO

The operative variable is amplitude of upper-body motion, not walking speed. Arms swinging from the shoulder rather than pinned to the ribs; torso permitted to rotate rather than held rigid; feet tracking slightly apart rather than on a single line.

Evidence: Johnson & Tassinary (PNAS, 2007), five studies, 700+ raters - shoulder swagger more than doubled attractiveness ratings for perceived men. A 2025 Scientific Reports 3D motion-capture study (52 walkers, 137 observers) converged on lateral torso oscillation and shoulder abduction as the predictors of perceived dominance. The pace literature is genuinely unresolved - the Chile/Germany/Russia replay study found the extremes rated highest, not the middle.
CUE 2 - HEAD AND CHEST
Open posture as a default, not as a pre-interview trick in a bathroom stall.

Evidence: the hormonal power-posing claims did not replicate (Ranehill et al., N=200; Carney herself disavowed the effect in 2016). What DID replicate is the self-reported feeling of power - meta-analyses across 40 and 117 studies find g = 0.35-0.40 on affective and self-directed outcomes. That felt-state effect is the mechanism you actually want, because it is what turns a posture you perform into a posture you have.
CUE 3 - HANDS OUT OF POCKETS
Every doorway. That is the trigger. Not a time of day, not a reminder app - doorways.
TRACK A - STRUCTURAL (2x/week, ~15 min, 8 weeks) - scheduled Monday & Thursday
Thoracic extension over a foam roller - 2x10, upper back only
Wall slides - 3x10, low back and forearms in contact
Chin tucks - 3x10, 5-second holds (deep neck flexors; the group nobody trains)
Doorway pec stretch - 2x30s each arm at three heights
Face pulls / band pull-aparts - 3x15
TRACK B - MOTOR LEARNING
Anchor to a cue, not a clock - doorways
Practice static, expect dynamic transfer
Film yourself - walking, seated, standing in a group. You will not believe it otherwise.
Brushing: Crest 3D Whitestrips Professional Effects - 20 treatments, 30 min/day
Sensodyne (potassium nitrate + fluoride) and a soft-bristled toothbrush. Start the Sensodyne a few days BEFORE treatment one.
Brush gently - soft brush, Sensodyne, 2 min. Floss. Rinse thoroughly; residue kills strip adhesion.
Pat teeth dry with a tissue. Dramatically improves adhesion.
Apply upper strip, then lower. Press along the tooth surface only - off the gumline.
Work. Sit through it. Do not double up on time or treatments.
Optional gentle brush; alcohol-free mouthwash if you want one.
Skincare: Three steps. Anything more is a hobby.
Water rinse (or gentle cleanser if oily) -> moisturizer -> broad-spectrum SPF 30+ on face, ears and neck. Two fingers' length is the dose most people underapply.
Gentle cleanser -> moisturizer. That is all.
Shower after every session. Watch the chest and back - that is where the acne shows up first on a bulk.
Shaving: Shower first, fresh blade, no pressure. That fixes most of it.
Shave after the shower, never before.
Use actual shave cream, not the foam in a pressurized can.
Zero pressure. Let the weight of the razor do it.
Short strokes, rinse constantly - two inches at a time, rinse the blade every stroke or two.
With the grain first. Re-lather before any second pass.
Go slower on the neck and accept less closeness.
Replace the blade every 5-7 shaves. Most irritation is a dull blade, not technique.
What you do not need: safety razors, straight razors, badger brushes, pre-shave oil. Enjoyable hobby, but it will not outperform a sharp cartridge used correctly.
Small grooming: Set it on a calendar. None of this survives on memory.
Book the next one when you leave.
Running: Rowing twice a week plus a daily hour of goalkeeping already puts nine cardio-ish sessions on the calendar. Adding runs on top would work directly against the 4,005 kcal surplus, which is the point of Phase 1. Revisit in Phase 2 if the scale is moving and recovery is fine.
